reads.macro_connection:
Jackson Hole was the inflection event this month. Warsh told markets the Fed may 'have work to do' — September hike odds jumped from 40% to 68% by month-end. The 10Y pushed to 4.75%, its highest since January 2025, and 30Y mortgage rates hit 6.66% (approaching the 2026 peak of 6.69%). Your fixed 3.75% mortgage is now the most valuable asset-class position on your balance sheet — the 291bp spread to market is locked and widening.

The small-bank funding picture that peaked in July continued to fade. TGA drain (Treasury building cash toward the $950B QRA target) is thinning reserves across the system. Your credit union's 4.01% APY held — they're still competing for deposits — but the environment is shifting. If the Fed hikes in September, your checking APY may follow upward (a rare case where a hike benefits you), but any variable-rate debt in the Lake Trust or Synchrony balances costs more immediately.

CPI at 3.4% was a slight reprieve from June's 3.5%, driven by falling gas prices in July. But US-Iran tensions are pushing oil back up — the next CPI print (August data, releasing Sep 11) may reverse the trend. Your real yield on checking stays positive but thin at +0.6%.
reads.monthly_note:
August 2026 was a split-personality month. On paper, the $720 deficit looks manageable. Under the hood, it was one of the most volatile months in the dataset.

The intra-month liquidity story is the real signal: checking balance hit $86.57 on August 5th — barely enough to clear a single debit card transaction — before the Charter Township paycheck rescued it to $2,102. It dropped to $198 on August 19th before the second Charter check rebuilt it to $2,266. And a third low point around August 12th saw the balance at $415 before the Guida paycheck arrived. The household is running three distinct paycheck-to-paycheck cycles within a single month.

The $2,944 Guida paycheck on 08/28 is the elephant in the room. If that was overtime, a bonus, or back pay, the income run-rate should be modeled at the normal ~$1,590 Guida level — which means a four-paycheck month like August would generate ~$7,673 in income, not $8,617. At $9,337 in spending, that's a -$1,664 structural deficit before the elevated check.

A northern Michigan road trip (Interlochen, Traverse City, Houghton Lake, West Branch, Grayling, Roscommon, Kingsley) ran roughly Aug 17-21 based on merchant locations. Trip-related spending: ~$225 in dining, ~$200 in gas and road stops, ~$165 in retail — roughly $590 in incremental spending the household wouldn't carry in a normal month.

Investment flow dropped to $444 (RH Brokerage only, no Schwab transfer) — a 5.2% savings rate, the lowest in the dataset. Debt service spiked to $916 on a $500 Lake Trust lump payment. Home Depot spending at $429 suggests an active home improvement project.

The forward question is whether the elevated Guida check repeats. If it does, September income could hold in the $8,500-9,000 range. If it reverts to ~$1,590, the household needs spending to drop below $8,000 to avoid a deeper deficit — and at the current run rate, that requires cutting ~$1,300 from the month. The most actionable levers: dining ($800 → $500 saves $300), groceries ($1,200 → $1,000 saves $200), and ATM cash ($1,500 → target $500 saves $1,000).
